judged_text: Every unauthenticated /embed/best request with an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, and the only gates — the Referer header check and the per-URL 60-second redis throttle — are both bypassable (referer is a client-spoofable header; the throttle is per-URL, so distinct URLs each get a fresh slot). A script hammering the endpoint with distinct embed_url values and a forged Referer makes the Discourse server create an unbounded number of topics under embed_by_username and fetch an unbounded number of pages from the partner host — unauthenticated topic-spam and outbound-fetch amplification.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds unauthenticated `GET /embed/best` (route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'`). In `EmbedController#best`, if `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)`; `current_user` can be nil, so any caller can enqueue jobs. The only request gate shown is `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`—a client-supplied Referer header. The job path (`RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#retrieve`) throttles via Redis key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` for 60s, which is per-URL; an attacker can vary `embed_url` paths on the allowed host to bypass it. `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` then calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` and ultimately `PostCreator` creates new topics/posts under `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` when the URL is new. This matches the finding: topic-spam + outbound fetch amplification is possible given settings are enabled.
